review_type: Single-agent targeted narrative synthesis, not a systematic review or exhaustive field search
reading_depth: All supplied PDFs: extracted text; abstract and available conclusion passages inspected. Extra selected methods inspected for F15 and F25. Added records have individual reading scopes. Not a claim of full line-by-line review.

arxiv_lookup.record_scope: Metadata only; retrieved latest version may differ from supplied PDF. arXiv year is submission year, not necessarily conference/journal year.

access_limits: Europe PMC two query attempts returned HTTP 503; no result counts or absence inference.

sources.read_scope: T: publisher text and archived primary-text passages; prior source ledger for ref.34

sources.title: Morano et al. (2025), Multimodal foundation model and benchmark for comprehensive retinal OCT image analysis (MIRAGE)
sources.read_scope: T: publisher abstract/introduction and indexed architecture/pretraining passages
sources.takeaway: OCT/SLO multimodal pretraining and a classification/segmentation benchmark are close prior work.
sources.boundary: OCT-only loading and pooling still need verification; our Base arm is not its headline Large configuration.

sources.title: Shi et al. (2025), A multimodal visual-language foundation model for computational ophthalmology (EyeCLIP)
sources.read_scope: T: publisher abstract/introduction and initial Results; prior plan records deeper review
sources.takeaway: Ophthalmic VLM with few-shot/zero-shot evaluations is an essential nearest-prior citation.
sources.boundary: This review did not re-audit every task-specific result; do not claim the first rare-eye FM application.

sources.title: Chen et al. (2026), Boosting foundation models for rare eye disease diagnosis via a multimodal text-to-image generative framework (EyeDiff)
sources.read_scope: T: archived full-text Introduction, Results and targeted Methods; live publisher redirect failed
sources.takeaway: Combines synthetic ophthalmic augmentation with foundation models, including OCT and rare-disease tasks.
sources.boundary: No first-ever synthetic-plus-retinal-FM claim; its protocols and results are not ours.

sources.title: Zhou et al. (2025), Generalist versus Specialist Vision Foundation Models for Ocular Disease and Oculomics
sources.read_scope: A: official arXiv abstract/record; preprint
sources.takeaway: Already compares generalist DINO variants with retinal specialists and examines adaptation/label efficiency.
sources.boundary: No inference about uninspected controls or universal specialist superiority; not a causal explanation of our future gaps.

sources.title: Lian et al. (2025), BenchReAD: A systematic benchmark for retinal anomaly detection
sources.read_scope: T: official conference abstract/metadata and paper section 2 excerpts
sources.takeaway: Retinal cross-dataset seen/unseen anomaly evaluation is established.

sources.read_scope: T: publisher abstract/dataset description and official Zenodo release/metadata fields

sources.title: Snell, Swersky and Zemel (2017), Prototypical Networks for Few-shot Learning
sources.read_scope: A: official proceedings abstract/metadata
sources.takeaway: Class means in a learned embedding motivate prototype-based classification.
sources.boundary: Our frozen pretrained embedding plus cosine centroids is not a newly meta-trained Prototypical Network.

sources.title: Wang et al. (2019), SimpleShot: Revisiting Nearest-Neighbor Classification for Few-Shot Learning
sources.read_scope: A: official arXiv abstract/metadata
sources.takeaway: Shows that simple feature transformations and nearest-neighbour baselines deserve serious comparison.
sources.boundary: Its centering/normalisation recipe is not identical to ours; do not add centering after seeing results.

sources.title: Guo et al. (2020), A Broader Study of Cross-Domain Few-Shot Learning
sources.read_scope: T: official paper benchmark/abstract excerpts and author project record
sources.takeaway: Includes satellite, dermatology and X-ray targets; highlights limits of within-domain few-shot rankings.
sources.boundary: Its tested fine-tuning/meta-learning ranking cannot establish a winner for our modern frozen encoders.

sources.read_scope: A: paper abstract, including official ICLR PDF excerpt
sources.takeaway: LP-FT addresses feature distortion in their transfer-learning settings.
sources.boundary: No universal sample threshold or guarantee for OCT; full-backbone adaptation stays outside this sprint.

sources.title: He et al. (2026), Boosting pathology foundation models via few-shot prompt-tuning for rare cancer subtyping (PathPT)
sources.read_scope: T: publisher abstract/introduction; indexed primary Methods/training/data-curation passages
sources.takeaway: Uses learned textual prompts, spatial aggregation and tile supervision for rare-cancer whole-slide classification.
sources.boundary: Not prompt tuning alone, not OCT, and not proof of scanner/staining invariance or feasibility on our Colab GPU.

sources.boundary: Headline accuracy is not comparable without a matched data/split/protocol audit; no new arm implied.

sources.title: Iwanicka and Lu (2026 proceedings; MIUA 2025), Diffusion with Adversarial Fine-Tuning for Improving Rare Retinal Disease Diagnosis
